story.head: A measuring-stick game
paras: The Senators (16-7-3) lost 5-3 to Florida on Wednesday, and the Lightning (15-7-2) lost 3-1 to Carolina the same night. Two good teams meet. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators first (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Lightning second (tied for seventh).

The Senators’ record (.673) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.610), largely because they’re 8-3 in one-goal games. The Lightning’s record (.667) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and keep dangerous shots away (3rd). On the other side, the Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd) and keep shots away from their net (3rd), but don’t block many shots (29th). Something has to give when the Bolts’ shooting runs into the Senators’ defense. Expect a chippy, heavy game.

Tim Stützle (13 G / 18 A / 31 P in 26 GP) leads the Senators in scoring, and Drake Batherson (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 26 GP) isn’t far behind. Nikita Kucherov (10 G / 23 A / 33 P in 24 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, and Jake Guentzel (13 G / 16 A / 29 P in 24 GP) has a team-high 13 goals.
Samuel Ersson (3-3-3 / .868 SV% in 8 GS) has struggled for Ottawa so far, but is expected to start. Dennis Hildeby (4-1-1 / .885 SV% in 6 GS) is expected to go for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Hagel, Cirelli and Goncalves out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Zetterlund, Stützle and Cozens.
